A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEAF research work. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-efficiency, classification, retrieval, image-generation and embedding-inversion experiments, with additional results and ablations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds VTAB, FLUX, bimodal-attack, transfer, typographic and token-level evaluations, plus BERT training results. Table 27 separately identifies imported baseline results.

M1.justification: The TextFARE objective, batched LEAF attack and semantic-constraint procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The BERT and FLUX experiments extend application of the approach without introducing a revised LEAF component or optimization rule.

E1.justification: v2 adds VTAB evaluation covering natural, specialized and structured tasks. It also introduces distinct testing scenarios involving combined image-and-text perturbations, token-level attacks and systematic typographic substitutions, substantially extending v1's evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: New retrieval Table 25 separately compares Original, vision-only robust FARE and LEAF; v1's retrieval tables compare original and bimodally robust models. New BERT Table 27 includes TextGrad alongside Original and Charmer reference results explicitly imported from earlier work. Existing main comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include FLUX.1-dev evaluation on 100 COCO images with only its CLIP encoder attacked, and retrieval attacks applying 100-step APGD at 2/255 and 4/255 after k=1 text perturbations. v2 also introduces BERT-base training on SST-2 and transfer-attack source/target configurations. Retained experiments keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds transferability analysis, typographic stress testing, bimodal retrieval attacks, TextFooler evaluations and the FLUX woman/woma case study. These substantially broaden robustness and failure analysis. The existing hyperparameter, embedding-collapse and adversarial-loss ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 7 specifies ten generation seeds for the new FLUX case study, and Table 27 adds a five-training-run averaging statement. The earlier three-seed experiment and existing plus/minus reporting remain. These additions do not establish increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their values, but substantial new results appear. Table 25 reports LEAF recall@1 of 43.4/42.8 versus FARE's 36.6/35.8 under the two bimodal attack radii. Table 28 reports only 1.70% AG-News TextFooler accuracy for both original and robust ViT-L/14. VTAB, FLUX, transfer, typographic and BERT results are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, expansion/contraction and replacement definitions, and mathematical reasoning remain unchanged. No substantive theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The main abstract and introduction claims remain stable. The revised conclusion explicitly extends potential applicability beyond CLIP to any text encoder, citing BERT, and strengthens clean-performance wording to 'intact' despite reported clean-performance losses.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly leaves attacks on both modalities unstudied; v2 discusses its sequential bimodal evaluation and instead identifies joint training as a possible improvement. It also establishes a token-level robustness limitation, discusses weak typographic robustness, and adds a tokenization-based interpretation of FLUX's woman/woma failure.

D1.justification: Table 6 adds the FLUX.1-dev checkpoint source. Appendix D.3 documents its encoder-access restriction and generation resolution, while Table 13 clarifies that retained SD-1.5/SDXL COCO results use all 5,000 validation images. Existing LEAF hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and code/model access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting FLUX, FLAN-T5, BERT, VTAB, the accuracy–robustness tradeoff and the CoAttack-style evaluation. Appendix C and the central positioning relative to FARE remain substantially unchanged; bibliographic corrections do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language and caption corrections, expands the conclusion and appendix roadmap, and adds subsections for the new analyses. Most original prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the publication footer is also updated.

P2.justification: Substantial new displays include the multi-seed FLUX Figure 7 and tables for VTAB, FLUX examples, transfer and typographic attacks, bimodal retrieval, BERT and token-level attacks. The COCO generation table gains a FLUX block. Older displays are largely preserved but repositioned and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 materially strengthens validation of the paper's central robustness claim: Table 25 addresses v1's explicit lack of bimodal-attack testing, while the token-level and typographic experiments reveal important failure boundaries. VTAB and FLUX further test applicability. The bimodal evidence concerns sequential attacks, and the conclusion overstates clean-performance preservation, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and understanding of limitations.
